What Is the Gary Brecka Sleep Optimization Challenge by The Ultimate Human

If you have been searching for the Gary Brecka sleep challenge, the 2 Day Sleep Reset, or the Ultimate Human Sleep Optimization Challenge, you are in the right place.

Gary Brecka of The Ultimate Human has launched a powerful sleep optimization challenge guide designed to help people fall asleep faster, stay asleep longer, and wake up feeling stronger. To perform better and better every day.

This is not just another sleep guide.

It is a structured system built around how your body actually works.

As a partner of Gary Brecka and The Ultimate Human, we are proud to support this challenge and the mission behind it.

Who Is Gary Brecka of The Ultimate Human

Gary Brecka is a human biologist, co-founder of The Ultimate Human, and a leader in performance and recovery optimization.

His work focuses on helping people understand how their bodies function so they can improve longevity, energy, health, and overall performance.

One of the most important areas he focuses on is sleep.

Not just getting more sleep, but improving the quality of sleep so the body can fully recover, repair, and perform.

The partnership between Gary Brecka and Matt Smith of Snooze Mattress Company is rooted in a real problem.

Gary discovered toxins in his bloodstream that were linked to his traditional mattress.

Like most people, he had never considered that the place he spends one third of his life could be impacting his health...his mattress.

Traditional mattresses often contain:

  • Flame-retardant chemicals

  • Petroleum-based foams

  • Plastics and Materials that release VOCs into the air

That means night after night, you are breathing in these compounds while your body is trying to recover.

Gary set out to find a better solution.

He connected with Matt Smith of Snooze Mattress Company to design a mattress that aligned with his biology.

The result was The Ultimate Snooze.

An organic, Sleep Toxin Free mattress and bedding system made without harmful chemicals and designed to support recovery at the highest level.

Since pre-launch in November 2025, we have been on a mission with Gary to help people wake up to their full potential every day through better sleep.

Our Shared Mission

Gary Brecka and The Ultimate Human focus on optimizing the body.

We focus on optimizing the environment.

Together, the mission is simple:

Help people improve performance through better sleep.

This includes:

  • Sleep adjustments and routines

  • Nervous system regulation

  • Reducing unnecessary stress on the body

When these are aligned, performance improves naturally.

Often immediately.

The guide highlights that your environment plays a major role in how well your body recovers.

Read our full Day 2 breakdown: Gary Brecka Sleep Challenge Day 2 — How to Deepen Sleep and Improve Recovery →

If you have ever asked, “Can I use my HSA or FSA for a mattress?” the answer is yes in certain cases.

Most mattresses do not qualify automatically. But if your sleep is affecting your health, including back pain, recovery, or overall wellness, you may be able to use HSA or FSA funds toward a better sleep setup.

Today, the easiest way to do this is through Truemed, which is integrated directly into our site and many other health-focused brands.

This guide walks through exactly how it works.

Can You Use HSA or FSA for a Mattress?

Yes, but only if it is considered medically necessary.

That means your mattress must support a health-related need such as:

  • Back or joint pain
  • Poor sleep quality
  • Recovery and performance issues
  • Mental or physical health

This is why many people turn to higher quality options like an organic latex mattress or a toxin free mattress. These are designed around support, alignment, and overall sleep quality rather than just comfort.

Why Truemed Makes This Process Easier

Traditionally, using HSA or FSA for a mattress required:

  • Visiting a doctor
  • Getting paperwork manually approved
  • Submitting documents yourself

With Truemed, the process is streamlined.

It allows you to:

  • Complete a quick health assessment online (<1min)
  • Get reviewed by a licensed provider
  • Receive a Letter of Medical Necessity if you qualify
  • Apply your HSA or FSA funds directly

Because Truemed is integrated into our and many other brands' checkout, the process happens as part of your purchase flow.

Step-by-Step: How to Use Truemed for Your Mattress

Step 1: Start at Checkout

When purchasing your mattress on our site, select the option to pay with HSA or FSA through Truemed.

Step 2: Complete the Truemed Assessment

You will be guided through a short questionnaire about your health and sleep.

This typically includes:

  • Sleep quality
  • Pain or discomfort
  • Any relevant health concerns

Step 3: Get Approved by a Licensed Provider

If eligible, a provider issues a Letter of Medical Necessity.

This is what allows your mattress to qualify under HSA or FSA guidelines.

Step 4: Complete Your Purchase

Once approved, you can proceed with your order using your HSA or FSA funds.

See the organic latex mattress designed for alignment, recovery, and a toxin free sleep environment.

Step 5: Payment or Reimbursement

Depending on your provider:

  • You may pay directly with your HSA or FSA card

The Traditional Route (Without Truemed)

It is still possible to qualify without Truemed, but it requires more effort.

You would need to:

  • Request a Letter of Medical Necessity
  • Submit paperwork manually to your HSA or FSA provider

This process can take more time and is less streamlined, which is why many people now use integrated platforms instead.

Why Mattress Materials Matter

Many traditional mattresses are made with:

  • Memory foam derived from petroleum
  • Chemical flame retardants

A chemical free mattress or organic latex mattress uses more natural materials such as:

  • Natural latex for long term support and pressure relief
  • Organic wool for airflow and temperature control

Sleep-focused experts like Gary Brecka often emphasize that your sleep environment plays a major role in recovery and long-term health. A chemically processed mattress can disrupt the recovery process by emitting toxins in the air you breathe. While organic mattresses eliminate the possibility. 

What to Look for in an HSA Eligible Mattress

If you are going through this process, it makes sense to choose something that supports long-term health and performance.

Look for:

  • Temperature regulation
  • Natural materials like wool and cotton help keep airflow consistent
  • Durability
  • Higher-quality materials tend to last longer than traditional foam mattresses
  • Free-Trial for risk-free assessment

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Most people spend their time trying to optimize diet and exercise.

They track calories. They follow workout plans. They buy supplements.

But they ignore the one thing they do every single night.

Sleep.

You will spend roughly one third of your life asleep. Yet it is often treated as an afterthought instead of the foundation of your health.

Sleep is not just recovery. It is regulation. It is repair. It is the system that allows everything else in your body to function properly.

Health experts like Gary Brecka consistently point to sleep as the starting point for performance, longevity, and overall well-being.

Sleep Is the Foundation of Everything

When sleep is off, everything else becomes harder.

Energy drops
Hormones become imbalanced
Recovery slows down
Focus declines

According to National Institutes of Health, sleep plays a critical role in brain function, physical health, and immune system performance.

The Sleep Foundation explains it simply. "Sleep is essential for survival. It impacts every system in the body."

This means your workouts, your diet, and your mental performance are all built on top of your sleep.

If sleep is weak, everything built on top of it is limited.

The Most Overlooked Habit

You can skip a workout.

You can miss a healthy meal.

But you cannot skip sleep.

You will sleep every night, whether it is good or bad.

That is what makes it the most powerful habit to improve.

If you upgrade something you do every single day for the rest of your life, the long-term impact compounds faster than anything else.

Most people focus on:

  • What they eat
  • How they train

Very few focus on:

  • What they sleep on
  • What they are breathing in for eight hours every night
  • Whether their sleep environment supports recovery

Your Sleep Environment Matters More Than You Think

Your body does not just respond to how long you sleep. It responds to the quality of that sleep.

One of the most overlooked factors is your mattress.

Traditional mattresses are often made with synthetic foams, adhesives, and materials that can trap heat and release compounds over time.

A toxin free mattress or organic latex mattress focuses on:

  • Materials that support a cleaner sleep environment
  • Non-Toxic Bedroom Air Quality

This is why the concept of a Gary Brecka organic mattress has gained attention. The idea is simple. If sleep drives recovery and longevity, then the environment you sleep in should support your biology, not work against it.

You can explore an example here:
https://theultimatesnooze.com/collections/mattress

Sleep Drives Recovery and Longevity

Sleep is where your body does its most important work.

During sleep:

  • Your brain processes and stores information
  • Your body repairs tissue
  • Hormones are regulated
  • Inflammation is reduced

The National Institutes of Health notes that sleep deficiency is linked to a higher risk of chronic conditions, including heart disease and metabolic issues.

This is why improving sleep is not just about feeling better the next day. It is about changing your long-term health trajectory.

Learn how to deepen these recovery stages: Gary Brecka Sleep Challenge Day 2 — How to Deepen Sleep and Improve Recovery →

The Simplest Way to Improve Your Health

Most health improvements require effort, discipline, and consistency.

Sleep is different.

You are already doing it.

The question is whether you are doing it well.

Improving sleep does not require more time. It requires better inputs.

That includes:

  • A consistent sleep schedule
  • A dark and quiet environment
  • A mattress that supports alignment and airflow

For those looking to take it further, upgrading to an organic latex mattress or toxin free mattress can be one of the most impactful changes because it affects every single night going forward.

You can also explore full sleep setups here:
https://theultimatesnooze.com/collections/bundle-ultimate-sleep-optimization-system

Why This Matters More Than Diet or Exercise Alone

Diet and exercise are important.

But they are limited without sleep.

Poor sleep can:

  • Increase cravings and hunger signals
  • Reduce physical performance
  • Slow recovery from workouts
  • Affect decision making

The Sleep Foundation highlights that sleep deprivation affects nearly every system in the body, including metabolism and cognitive function.

That means you can be doing everything right during the day, but if your sleep is off, you are working against yourself.

Start With What You Do Every Night

If you want the highest return on your health, start with sleep.

It is the one habit that:

  • Happens every day

The goal is not perfection. It is improvement.

Take the First Step

If you are shopping for a mattress, you are likely comparing comfort levels, firmness, and price. What most people overlook is what the mattress is actually made of.

The materials inside your mattress directly affect how you sleep, how your body recovers, and what you are exposed to every night. This is where the difference between organic latex and memory foam becomes important.

What Is Inside a Traditional Memory Foam Mattress

Memory foam is one of the most common materials used in modern mattresses. It is popular because it is inexpensive to produce and creates a soft, contouring feel.

Memory foam is typically made from polyurethane, a petroleum-based material. To achieve its signature feel, manufacturers often add chemical agents that affect density, heat retention, and response time.

Many memory foam mattresses also include adhesives to bond layers together, flame retardants to meet safety standards, and synthetic covers or blends.

These materials can release volatile organic compounds, especially when the mattress is new — a process known as off-gassing. The United States Environmental Protection Agency explains that volatile organic compounds can contribute to indoor air pollution and may cause symptoms such as headaches, dizziness, and irritation, depending on exposure levels. (Source: EPA)

What Is Inside an Organic Latex Mattress

An organic latex mattress is built using materials that are closer to their natural state and processed with fewer chemical inputs.

At The Ultimate Snooze, the construction focuses on three primary materials: organic cotton in the cover for breathability and softness, organic wool for temperature regulation and as a natural fire barrier, and natural latex for top-level pressure relief and comfort.

Latex is derived from the sap of rubber trees and processed into a resilient foam. Unlike memory foam, it does not rely on petroleum as its base.

The mattress is then built using a hybrid design with pocketed coils — adding structural support, improving airflow, and helping maintain proper spinal alignment.

You can explore both models here:

  • Pure Organic Latex Mattress — GOLS-certified latex, 800 pocketed coils, organic cotton and wool, zero off-gassing
  • Pillowtop Organic Mattress — same certified materials with an added organic pillowtop layer for a softer feel

How Materials Impact Your Sleep Quality

Sleep is a biological process that depends on the body entering a state of safety and recovery.

Gary Brecka often explains that sleep is not just about feeling tired. It is about the nervous system shifting into a state where cortisol drops and melatonin rises. Your sleep environment plays a role in this process.

Materials that trap heat, restrict airflow, or introduce chemical exposure can create subtle stress on the body. Materials that breathe well, regulate temperature, and reduce unnecessary inputs can support deeper sleep.

THE MATERIAL DIFFERENCE

Memory foam is petroleum-based. Our mattresses use certified organic latex, cotton, and wool — no synthetic foam, no chemical adhesives, no fiberglass.

Compare Our Mattresses →

Latex vs Memory Foam: Key Differences

Temperature regulation

Memory foam tends to trap heat because of its dense structure, leading to overheating during the night.

Natural latex is more breathable and — combined with a hybrid coil system — allows for better airflow and temperature balance. Paired with organic cotton sheets, the temperature difference is noticeable from the first night.

Durability

Memory foam can break down over time, leading to sagging and loss of support. Natural latex is more resilient and maintains its structure for a longer period — which is why The Ultimate Snooze Pure Mattress carries a 30-year warranty.

Responsiveness

Memory foam creates a sinking feeling and slow response when changing positions. Latex responds quickly and provides more balanced support without trapping the body.

Material composition

Memory foam is derived from synthetic petroleum-based materials. Natural latex comes from a renewable source and is combined with organic cotton and wool in higher quality builds.

Chemical exposure

Memory foam mattresses often include additives and adhesives that can off-gas. Organic latex mattresses focus on reducing chemical inputs and using more natural components.

The Role of Flame Retardants and Additives

Flame retardants are required for safety, but how they are implemented matters.

Some conventional mattresses rely on chemical flame retardants, while others use natural materials like wool that meet fire standards without added chemicals. Research from the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences has explored how certain flame retardants may impact hormone function and overall health. (Source: NIEHS)

This is one of the reasons many people look for mattresses that use natural fire barriers — like the organic New Zealand wool used in every Ultimate Snooze mattress.

Why Hybrid Construction Matters

Beyond materials, construction plays a major role in how a mattress performs. The Ultimate Snooze uses a hybrid design that combines natural latex with pocketed coils. This provides targeted support through individual coils, improved airflow compared to solid foam cores, better durability over time, and more balanced pressure relief without excessive sinking.

Which One Is Better for Long-Term Health

The answer depends on your priorities.

If your focus is short-term comfort at a lower price point, memory foam may meet that need.

If your focus is long-term durability, reduced chemical exposure, and a sleep environment aligned with recovery, organic latex is a stronger option. Sleep is one of the few activities you repeat every day for hours at a time. Small differences in materials can compound over years.

The Ultimate Snooze Approach

The Ultimate Snooze was designed in partnership with Gary Brecka to align with a performance-driven approach to sleep. Instead of focusing only on feel, the design prioritizes organic materials, hybrid support, and reduced reliance on synthetic foams and adhesives.

Pure Organic Latex Mattress

GOLS-certified organic latex, 800 pocketed coils, organic cotton and wool, hand-tufted — no petroleum foam, no fiberglass, no chemical adhesives. 30-year warranty.

Pillowtop Organic Mattress

All the same certified materials as the Pure with an organic pillowtop layer for a plusher feel — still zero synthetic foam.

Complete Bedding Bundle

Organic sheets, pillows, and a mattress protector — all certified, all designed to complement the mattress for a fully chemical-free sleep surface.

READY TO SWITCH FROM FOAM?

Explore our certified organic latex mattresses

Shop Organic Mattresses → View Complete Bundles →

Frequently Asked Questions

Is organic latex better than memory foam for sleep?
Organic latex tends to provide better airflow, durability, and a more responsive feel compared to memory foam.

Do memory foam mattresses release chemicals?
Many memory foam mattresses release volatile organic compounds, especially when new. The level varies by brand and materials used.

Are organic mattresses worth the investment?
For people focused on long-term sleep quality and reducing chemical exposure, organic mattresses can offer meaningful benefits.

Does latex sleep cooler than memory foam?
Yes, natural latex combined with breathable materials and a hybrid design typically allows for better temperature regulation.

Final Thoughts

Most mattress comparisons focus on comfort and price. The real difference is in what you are sleeping on every night. Materials matter. Construction matters. And over time, those choices influence how well your body recovers.

If you are looking to upgrade your sleep environment, start by exploring what’s inside an organic latex mattress. That is where the real difference begins.

What Is the Difference Between King and California King?

The biggest misconception is that a California King is larger than a standard King in every way.

It is not.

A standard King, often called an Eastern King, is wider. A California King is longer.

Standard King dimensions
76 inches wide by 80 inches long

California King dimensions
72 inches wide by 84 inches long

You are trading width for length.

That means the total surface area is nearly identical. The shape is just different.

This is why many people order a California King thinking they are getting more space, when in reality they are getting less width.

Which Mattress Is Better for Couples

For most couples, width matters more than length.

A standard King gives each person more personal space side to side. This is especially important if:

  • You or your partner move during the night
  • You share the bed with a pet or child
  • You prefer space between you while sleeping

A King mattress is often the better choice for comfort and flexibility.

If your goal is maximizing usable sleep space, the extra width usually wins.

Who Should Choose a California King

A California King is ideal for specific situations.

It works best if:

  • You are taller than six feet
  • You feel cramped at the foot of the bed
  • Your bedroom layout is narrower and longer

For taller individuals, the added four inches of length can make a noticeable difference in comfort.

For everyone else, the reduced width can feel like a downgrade.

Is California King the Biggest Mattress

No, and this is one of the most searched questions.

A California King is not the biggest mattress available.

There are larger sizes such as:

  • Alaskan King
  • Wyoming King
  • Texas King

For example, an Alaskan King can measure up to 108 inches by 108 inches, making it significantly larger than both King and California King options.

These are typically niche products designed for large families or luxury spaces.

Which Mattress Is Best for Families

If you have kids who occasionally climb into bed or you want maximum space, a standard King is usually the best choice.

The added width allows for:

  • More room for multiple sleepers
  • Less disturbance from movement
  • Greater overall comfort

If your family regularly co sleeps, you may even consider oversized options like Alaskan King, but these require custom frames and bedding.

For most households, a King provides the best balance.

Watch Out for Bed Frame Compatibility

One of the most common mistakes people make is ordering the wrong mattress size for their bed frame.

A California King will not properly fit a standard King frame.

A King will not properly fit a California King frame.

Before purchasing, always confirm:

  • Your current bed frame size
  • Room dimensions
  • Sheet and bedding compatibility

This is a simple step that can prevent major frustration.

Why Mattress Materials Matter Just as Much as Size

Choosing the right size is important, but what your mattress is made of matters just as much.

You spend hours every night in direct contact with your mattress. Materials impact:

  • Temperature regulation
  • Airflow
  • Support and pressure relief
  • Chemical exposure

Many traditional mattresses use synthetic foams and adhesives that can release volatile organic compounds.

The United States Environmental Protection Agency explains that these compounds can contribute to indoor air pollution and affect air quality over time
https://www.epa.gov/indoor-air-quality-iaq/volatile-organic-compounds-impact-indoor-air-quality

This is why more people are looking for organic and non chemical alternatives.

What If You Need More Than a King or California King? The Split King Option

If the reason you are looking at California King — or even bigger — is because you and a partner have different sleep needs, there is a better solution worth knowing about: the Split King.

A Split King uses two Twin XL mattresses (38 inches wide by 80 inches long each) placed side by side. Together they create the same 76-by-80-inch footprint as a standard King — but each side operates completely independently.

Each person controls their own head and foot incline on separate adjustable bases. One partner can elevate to read or relieve back pressure while the other stays flat. There is zero motion transfer between the two sides.

For couples where one person is a light sleeper, has back pain, or prefers a different position than their partner, a Split King setup often solves the problem that a bigger mattress cannot.

The Ultimate Snooze Core™ and Elite™ bundles are both available in Split King configuration, pairing organic latex mattresses with adjustable bases designed for independent movement on each side.

Explore Split King bundles at The Ultimate Snooze →

The Ultimate Snooze Approach to King and California King

At The Ultimate Snooze, both King and California King options are available, built with a focus on performance and recovery.

Each mattress is designed in partnership with Gary Brecka and built using:

  • Organic cotton for breathability
  • Organic wool for temperature regulation
  • Natural latex for responsive support
  • A hybrid pocketed coil system for airflow and durability

This combination supports deeper sleep by aligning with how the body recovers, not just how the mattress feels.

You can explore available King and California King options here
https://theultimatesnooze.com

Quick Size Comparison Summary

Choose a standard King if you want more width, more space for couples, and flexibility for families.

Choose a California King if you need extra legroom and are taller or working with a narrower bedroom layout.

Consider a Split King if you and a partner have different sleep positions, firmness preferences, or schedules — and want each person to have independent control.

Avoid choosing based on the assumption that California King is bigger overall.

It is simply longer, not larger.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between King and California King mattress
A King is wider while a California King is longer. The total area is similar but the shape is different.

Is California King bigger than King
No. It is longer but narrower, so it is not bigger overall.

Which mattress is better for couples
A standard King is usually better because it provides more width and personal space. For couples with different sleep needs, a Split King on adjustable bases provides independent control for each person.

Is California King the biggest mattress
No. Larger options like Alaskan King exist, but they are specialty sizes. For most couples wanting more individual space, a Split King is the more practical upgrade.

Can I use King sheets on a California King
No. The dimensions are different, so you will need the correct bedding for each size.

What is a Split King
Two Twin XL mattresses side by side on separate adjustable bases, creating a King footprint where each side moves independently.

Final Thoughts

Most people focus on choosing between King and California King based on what sounds bigger.

The better approach is to choose based on how you sleep.

If you want width, choose Standard (Eastern) King.
If you need length, choose California King.
If you and a partner have different needs, consider a Split King.

And once you choose the right size, the next step is making sure the materials you are sleeping on support your health and recovery every night.

That is where the real upgrade happens.
